body_html:
Virginia has enacted 5 AI-related laws. Each is read from its enrolled text: what it does, who it applies to, when it takes effect, and what it requires.

Enacted AI laws in Virginia

5 laws this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • HB1186: Artificial intelligence; use of systems for student instruction. passed 2026-04-13

    The law requires the Virginia Department of Education to compile information on current uses of artificial intelligence systems for student instruction and to post guidance for safe, ethical, and equitable use of AIS in public elementary and secondary schools. It requires each school board to adopt policies consistent with that guidance. It also establishes the AIS Innovation in Education Pilot Program to fund and evaluate AIS uses in schools, with the Pilot Program expiring July 1, 2030.

  • SB394: Artificial intelligence; use of systems for student instruction. passed 2026-04-13

    Requires the Virginia Department of Education to compile information on current AIS uses in public schools and post guidance for safe, ethical, and equitable use of AIS in instructional settings. Requires each school board to establish, implement, and enforce policies consistent with that guidance. Establishes the AIS Innovation in Education Pilot Program to fund, evaluate, and scale safe and innovative AIS uses in public elementary and secondary schools, with the Pilot Program provisions expiring July 1, 2030.

  • HB580: Consumer Counsel, Division of; establishing mechanisms for receiving and investigating complaints. passed 2026-04-06

    The law amends Section 2.2-517 of the Code of Virginia to expand the duties of the Division of Consumer Counsel. It adds a requirement that the Division establish mechanisms for receiving and investigating consumer complaints involving emerging technologies, including referring appropriate complaints to federal, state, and local enforcement agencies. It also retains existing duties such as operating a consumer hotline, resolving complaints, and maintaining public records.

  • HB171: Student instruction; Internet safety, policy to include key modern digital safety topics. passed 2026-04-02

    Requires each local school board in Virginia to review and approve an acceptable internet use policy every two years, with minimum provisions including filtering or blocking child pornography and obscenity, prohibiting illegal material, establishing measures against violators, and providing internet safety instruction on online scams, misinformation, and artificial intelligence generated content. It also requires certain private schools to filter or block child pornography and obscenity, and directs the Superintendent of Public Instruction to issue guidelines on the required internet safety topics.

  • HJR32: Higher educational institutions; JLARC to study artificial intelligence use policies. passed 2026-03-03

    Directs the Joint Legislative Audit and Review Commission to study artificial intelligence use policies at institutions of higher education in Virginia, survey and evaluate those policies, develop a model policy, and make recommendations for AI tools, curricula, and resources. The study must be completed by November 30, 2027, with an executive summary submitted by the first day of the 2028 Regular Session.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for Virginia. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
